learningObjectives: Select and justify data encryption in a business scenario.
Select and justify field-level auditing in a business scenario.
reviewScope: Official topic comparison and original-question editorial review; not vendor endorsement.

elements.description: Encryption protects sensitive persisted data using managed cryptographic keys. Individual properties and BLOB data can have different encryption configurations; consider exposed columns as well as serialized data. Password hashing is a different, irreversible mechanism. Encryption does not replace authorization or safe key handling.

elements.text: Worked example: Protect a sensitive account field and review its exposed-column storage as well as the case BLOB. Manage keys securely and verify that only authorized paths can obtain readable data.

elements.description: Standard case history records actions; field-level auditing records configured field changes, including old/new values, actor and time. Enable auditing for relevant fields and inspect embedded data fields when needed. Auditing is evidence after a change, not a mechanism that blocks the change.

elements.text: Worked example: Audit a dispatch address so investigators can see who changed it and when. Keep access to the audit record appropriate because it can contain previous sensitive values.

elements.title: Training environment checklist
items: Implement the worked example in a training application; use synthetic data.
Test the expected path and at least one failure or boundary condition.
Explain why the alternative mechanism would not meet the requirement.
Revisit incorrect answers in Smart Review rather than memorizing option positions.

elements.text: These notes target the '25 exam. Shared Academy pages may show newer labels with '25 applicability; verify screens in your training environment.

examPitfalls.title: Hash versus encryption
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A password hash is decrypted to authenticate a user.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Hashing is distinct from reversible data encryption.

examPitfalls.title: Audit versus permission
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Enabling field auditing prevents unauthorized edits.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use authorization for prevention and auditing for traceability.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An encrypted case BLOB is introduced. Why should exposed sensitive columns still be reviewed?

options.text: A BLOB is only a browser cache
They may store values outside that serialized BLOB
All exposed columns cease to exist automatically
Encryption grants every user access

practiceQuiz.rationale: Protect the actual storage locations. BLOB encryption is not a blanket proof that every separately exposed value is protected.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: A BLOB is serialized Case storage, not just browser cache.
optionExplanations.B: Exposed columns may persist values outside the encrypted BLOB.
optionExplanations.C: Encryption does not delete exposed columns.
optionExplanations.D: Encryption does not grant application access.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which statement correctly distinguishes password hashing from encryption?

options.text: Hashing is irreversible; encryption is designed to be reversible with appropriate keys
Every hash is decrypted using the username
Encryption has no keys
Both are only display masks

practiceQuiz.rationale: The two mechanisms serve different requirements. Password verification does not require recovering a plaintext password.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: Hashes support verification; encryption supports keyed recovery.
optionExplanations.B: A password hash is not decrypted using a username.
optionExplanations.D: Both affect representation beyond a visual mask.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO concerns remain after sensitive data is encrypted?

options.text: How cryptographic keys are managed
A need to publish keys in user logs
A guarantee that all users can read the data
Who is authorized to read decrypted values

practiceQuiz.rationale: Encryption protects stored representation but key access and application authorization still determine exposure.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: Key handling governs access to protected data.
optionExplanations.C: Encryption does not authorize every reader.
optionExplanations.D: Decrypted values still need authorization controls.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A field is visually masked in a portal. Which conclusion is unsafe?

options.text: Storage configuration should be inspected
Authorization still matters
Its persisted database value is necessarily encrypted
The UI hides some displayed characters

practiceQuiz.rationale: Presentation masking does not prove encryption at rest. Verify the property and actual persistence configuration.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

optionExplanations.C: A display mask does not prove stored encryption.
optionExplanations.D: Masking describes the visible presentation only.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team must identify who changed a case's delivery address and its previous value. Which feature fits?

options.text: A ruleset prerequisite
Field-level auditing
Only a portal logo
A connector timeout setting

practiceQuiz.rationale: Field-level audit entries capture actor, time and changed values for configured fields.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: Prerequisites describe rule dependencies, not edit history.
optionExplanations.B: Field auditing captures the actor and value changes.
optionExplanations.C: A logo does not record changes.
optionExplanations.D: Timeout configuration does not record field edits.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO are expected in a field-change audit record?

options.text: Old and new field values
Who made the change and when
A guarantee that the change was correct
The browser's theme color

practiceQuiz.rationale: Audit records provide traceability. They do not establish business correctness merely because an action was recorded.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: Previous and new values support change tracing.
optionExplanations.B: Actor and time identify the edit event.
optionExplanations.C: Recording an edit does not prove its correctness.
optionExplanations.D: Theme color is unrelated to the change record.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Standard case history records routing and status changes. What should be configured to track a specific embedded field?

options.text: Nothing; every property is audited by default
Only the assignment deadline
A new mock exam
Field-level auditing for the relevant embedded field

practiceQuiz.rationale: Detailed field auditing is configured explicitly; general case action history is not the same as a full record of every property edit.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: General history does not audit every field automatically.
optionExplanations.B: Deadline configuration does not capture the field's edits.
optionExplanations.C: A mock exam has no persistence audit role.
optionExplanations.D: Configure the relevant field explicitly for auditing.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Does field-level auditing prevent an unauthorized user from changing a value?

options.text: Yes; audit dates lock the case permanently
Only if the new value is shorter
No; permissions must prevent unauthorized changes
Yes; auditing replaces all roles

practiceQuiz.rationale: Auditing records changes. Authorization is the preventive control.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: Audit records do not create a permanent edit lock.
optionExplanations.B: Value length does not determine authorization.
optionExplanations.D: Auditing provides traceability, not a replacement for roles.

quickRecap.value: Encryption protects sensitive persisted data using managed cryptographic keys. Individual properties and BLOB data can have different encryption configurations; consider exposed columns as well as serialized data. Password hashing is a different, irreversible mechanism. Encryption does not replace authorization or safe key handling.

Standard case history records actions; field-level auditing records configured field changes, including old/new values, actor and time. Enable auditing for relevant fields and inspect embedded data fields when needed. Auditing is evidence after a change, not a mechanism that blocks the change.
